title: Content Is Code - Matt Palmer, Conductor
talk_summary: A DevRel talk arguing that code (React/TypeScript/Remotion) is now the cheapest medium for producing content assets, and that the real bottleneck is structure and conscientiousness rather than coding skill.

takeaways.technique: Structured source-of-truth repos as agent substrate
takeaways.what_they_do: Keeps design tokens, brand guidelines, and front-end/back-end separation explicit in the repo so generated assets stay consistent instead of drifting into generic output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all the assets that I showed you at the beginning of this video are a byproduct of design tokens, structured code

takeaways.technique: Curated skills/docs instead of auto-generated ones
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues agents fail without accurate internal documentation and skills, and that most skills are generated with no regard for content or structure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Even if you have really good agents, they're not going to know how to solve these problems if they don't have documentation or skills

takeaways.technique: PR hygiene as review input (tags, descriptions, revert tracking)
takeaways.what_they_do: Calls out that almost no org tags PRs, writes real descriptions, or distinguishes feature vs bugfix vs revert, which breaks downstream understanding.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Tagging PRs, PR descriptions, knowing what's a feature and what's a bug fix, knowing if you reverted a PR

takeaways.what_they_do: Claims output quality now depends more on meticulous process and organizational rigor than on model or engineer skill.
takeaways.evidence_quote: AI rewards conscientiousness. AI rewards organizational excellence. AI rewards structure.
